title: Barossa and Eden Valley
subtitle: Warm valley, cool hills
objectives: Compare it with the Barossa Valley

steps.title: Eden Valley
steps.body: Eden Valley lies in the hills east of the Barossa Valley, at about 400 to 600 m. It's cooler, windier and wetter, with granite and schist soils. It's part of the Barossa zone but a separate GI. Its wines are fresher and more elegant than the valley floor's.

steps.title: Riesling and Shiraz
steps.body: Eden Valley is famous for dry Riesling: lime, lemon and floral when young, developing toast and honey with age. Its Shiraz is more peppery and elegant than Barossa Valley Shiraz. Henschke's Hill of Grace, from Shiraz vines planted around 1860, is one of Australia's most famous wines.

steps.prompt: What makes Eden Valley cooler than the Barossa Valley?

steps.body: Hill of Grace takes its name from the Lutheran church across the road, Gnadenberg, meaning hill of grace.

steps.explanation: Eden Valley is cool and hilly.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Eden Valley is higher and cooler, in the eastern hills
It's famous for dry Riesling and elegant Shiraz
Henschke's Hill of Grace comes from 1860 vines
